source_name: BQK press/news section (Albanian) — provenance anchor for media figures
source_subtype: central bank press release feed (pointer for media triangulation)
why_relevant: Not a media source, but the anchor every Kosovo Albanian outlet cites: monthly 'Publikimi i statistikave të bankave komerciale' releases are the origin of most media figures. Needed to date-check and de-duplicate journalistic numbers; also names the exact Albanian phrasing outlets reuse.

source_name: JOQ Albania (joq-albania.com)
why_relevant: High-reach Albanian-language aggregator/portal that republishes Kosovo banking-credit stories; useful only as a reach indicator and mirror. Editorial standards are low — never use as a figure source without tracing to origin.

source_name: KALKULO KREDI (kalkulokredi.com) — Kosovo loan rate comparison
why_relevant: Albanian-language commercial comparison site listing Kosovo banks' advertised loan interest rates. Not media, but it is a market-facing data surface that reveals bank-level pricing which media then quote; complements the aggregate BQK interest-rate series.

source_name: Bank tariff/price-list disclosures surfaced via Albanian media and search (e.g. BKT Kosova çmimorja)
why_relevant: Kosovo banks publish dated Albanian-language 'Çmimorja' (fee schedule) PDFs covering card issuance, ATM withdrawal and POS fees. Media frequently cite these when reporting fee changes; they are the ground truth for card/ATM pricing that no aggregate statistic carries.

source_name: TEB SHA Kosova — FAQ / customer-information pages (sq)
why_relevant: Bank self-published Albanian FAQ describing card products, ATM/POS usage rules and limits. Useful for the Albanian terminology bank customers and journalists actually use, and for spotting product/network changes referenced in media.

source_name: UBT Knowledge Center (knowledgecenter.ubt-uni.net) — Albanian theses on Kosovo banking
why_relevant: Open repository of Albanian-language theses ('Sistemi bankar në Kosovë') that compile historical branch/ATM/card series and often reproduce data obtained directly from banks or BQK for years no longer available online. Excellent for back-series reconstruction.

source_name: BQK official Facebook page (bqk.ks)
why_relevant: BQK announces regulatory/methodological changes (e.g. the Methodological Instruction for data reporting in the credit-registry system) on social media, sometimes with detail or timing not mirrored on the website; Albanian media routinely pick stories up from here.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — Platni sistem / Statistika
why_relevant: Serbia's central bank publishes quarterly payment-services statistics (cards issued, acceptance network, ATM and POS data, cash vs cashless transfers, e-money, internet purchases) in Excel/PDF. Serbia-wide rather than Kosovo-specific, but it is the only authoritative counterpart series for the dinar-denominated payment channels that serve Serbian-majority municipalities, and it is the baseline against which parallel-channel flows must be read.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — saopštenja o dinaru na Kosovu i Metohiji
why_relevant: NBS press/Q&A items are the issuing authority's own account of the ban on dinar cash entry into Kosovo, cash-transport arrangements (Leposavić treasury, Jarinje crossing, licensed CIT carrier), and volumes/purposes of dinar funds sent for salaries, pensions and social benefits. Primary institutional commentary on parallel cash channels.

source_name: KoSSev — informativni portal sa severa Kosova
why_relevant: The reference Serbian-language newsroom based in North Mitrovica. Reports operationally on bank branch openings/closures in the north, Poštanska štedionica payout arrangements, dinar shortages, child/parental allowance and social-benefit payment days — the granular payments reality of Serbian-majority municipalities that no Albanian- or English-language outlet covers at this resolution.

source_name: Kosovo Online — sekcija Ekonomija / Analize
why_relevant: Belgrade-linked Serbian-language portal covering Kosovo with a dedicated economy section; carries regulatory changes affecting payments (e.g. the cash-payment threshold above which transactions must go through a bank), dinar-ban analyses, and expert commentary on monetary/payment rules between Serbia and Kosovo. High-volume pointer to statements, officials and rulebooks.

source_name: Radio KIM (Čaglavica/Gračanica) — analize i vesti
why_relevant: Serbian-language broadcaster/portal serving central-Kosovo Serbian enclaves (Gračanica area), not just the north. Publishes analysis on the practical effects of the dinar abolition on households, and is one of the few sources covering enclaves south of the Ibar where banking access differs from Mitrovica.

source_name: Banka Qendrore e Republikës së Kosovës (CBK) — srpska jezička verzija sajta
why_relevant: The Kosovo central bank publishes its statistics pages, Financial Stability Reports and Annual Reports in a Serbian-language version (?lang=sr). This is the regulator-side counterpart to Belgrade sources: licensing of banks operating in the north, cash/currency rules, and the payments-statistics series. Critical for this cell because Serbian-language readers and northern actors cite these documents.

source_name: Banka Poštanska štedionica a.d. Beograd
why_relevant: Reported as effectively the only Serbian bank still operating dinar services for Kosovo clients, running branches in the north plus prefabricated branches at the Jarinje, Brnjak, Končulj and Merdare crossings with capped daily cash withdrawals. Its branch network, working hours and withdrawal limits are the single best proxy for parallel-channel banking access; annual reports and network pages are the primary artifacts.

source_name: Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju, Vlada Republike Srbije
why_relevant: The Serbian government body that organises and announces payment of salaries, pensions and social transfers to Serbs in Kosovo, and coordinated the crossing-point branch arrangement. Its announcements are the closest thing to official volumetrics on the parallel payment channel (beneficiary counts, payout schedules, affected categories).

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL) — Balkanski servis, Kosovo
why_relevant: Serbian-language RFE/RL reporting is the most methodical cross-checked source on dinar shortages in Serbian-majority areas, cash-transport incidents at crossings, and how households actually move money. Frequently the only outlet that interviews both Belgrade and Pristina institutions on the same payments question.

source_name: Danas — rubrika Ekonomija (Kosovo/dinar coverage)
why_relevant: Belgrade daily whose economy desk carries economist commentary quantifying the dinar ban's reach (tens of thousands of salary/pension/social-benefit recipients) and the conversion-cost mechanics of dinar-to-euro. Useful for expert names to snowball into direct analytic sources.

source_name: Vreme — ekonomija (Kosovo dinar circulation reporting)
why_relevant: Serbian weekly with reported pieces on whether the dinar remains in de-facto circulation in Serbian municipalities after the ban, and on the crossing-point branch scheme. Valuable because it tests official claims against observed behaviour — the informal-usage dimension that statistics miss.

source_name: New Social Initiative (NSI) — Mitrovica-based think tank
why_relevant: Kosovo Serb civil-society research organisation based in North Mitrovica, publishing policy analysis on the position of the Serb community including economic and service-access dimensions. One of very few analytic (not journalistic) sources produced from inside the Serbian-majority north; publishes in Serbian and English.

source_name: Radio Gorazdevac / Gorazdevac Media Group
why_relevant: Serbian-language outlet operating since 1999 from the Peć/Pejë-area enclave, a BIRN partner with an established online presence. Covers the western enclaves whose banking access and cash logistics differ sharply from the contiguous north — a geographic sub-cell otherwise unrepresented.

source_name: Politika — Kosovo i Metohija economic coverage
why_relevant: Serbia's paper of record; reliably carries the official Belgrade framing and the operational detail of state-organised payment arrangements for Kosovo Serbs (branch placements, transfer mechanics). Useful as a record of the institutional position, to be read against Pristina-side sources.

source_name: Nova Ekonomija (Belgrade business magazine)
why_relevant: Serbian business/finance magazine that covers payments, cash and the informal economy analytically (e.g. shadow-economy share of GDP series). Relevant as the Serbian-language venue where quantified cash-usage and informal-payment analysis is published and where NALED/other research is first reported.

source_name: NALED — Suzbijanje sive ekonomije (cashless/shadow-economy programme)
why_relevant: Serbian public-private alliance that produces the recurring shadow-economy measurement (share of GDP) and cashless-payment advocacy research with donor backing. The methodology and series are the main Serbian-language quantitative reference on cash intensity, transferable as context for dinar-cash behaviour in Serbian-majority areas.

source_name: NLB Komercijalna banka — Kosovska Mitrovica branch network (Serbian-serving retail)
why_relevant: Pointer to the commercial-bank layer serving Serbian clients: reporting describes a Kosovska Mitrovica branch with multiple outposts across Kosovo and Metohija, a five-figure client base, and dual-currency ATM withdrawal — a rare concrete datapoint on ATM currency configuration in Serbian-majority areas. Use as a lead into the bank's own disclosures and CBK licensing records rather than as an authority itself.

source_name: Javni servis (javniservis.net) — long-form Serbian analysis
why_relevant: Serbian-language analytical/long-form outlet carrying essayistic treatment of the dinar removal and its social-payments consequences. Lower authority but useful for framing, actor names and the lived mechanics of parallel payment channels.

source_name: JuGmedia — south Serbia / Kosovo border-area regional portal
why_relevant: Regional Serbian-language outlet covering the Preševo/Bujanovac–Kosovo border zone, where the Merdare and Končulj crossing-point banking arrangements sit. Covers cross-boundary cash movement and the currency question from the Serbia-proper side of the boundary.

source_name: Riinvest Institute — Publications (Publikimet)
why_relevant: Kosovo's leading independent economic think tank; runs its own enterprise and household surveys and is the standard reference for informal-economy / undeclared-income estimates (e.g. ~34.4% of firm income unreported, 2013), which are the closest available proxy for cash-intensity of the Kosovo economy. Publication list is Albanian-first with PDFs served from a predictable /uploads/files/YYYY/Month/DD/ path.
